answer: Quartz-timestamp fingerprint auditing. Each agent action embeds a coarse hash of its recent call history; auditors cluster identical histories across supposedly unrelated accounts. Accounts sharing a fingerprint below a set entropy floor are merged and their rewards clawed back. Attackers must pay one fresh, behaviorally distinct runtime per identity—ongoing compute plus harbor warm-up, not a one-time fee. A karst-like delay in reward finality (weeks) makes the fleet costly to sustain before detection.
